forecaster_note: Tue: light to moderate S/SW at dawn, cleanish on the Northern Beaches but no real swell — waist high at best on the south magnets; short-period S swell picks up through the day and winds go onshore with rain, lumpy and unappealing. Wed: strong southerly gusts and a spike of short-period S swell — S exposures well overhead to 2x OH mess, only waist-high at sheltered Sth corners, chest to head at slightly more exposed ones. Thu: S swell stays overhead on S exposures, chance of a SW window at dawn then SE lump. Fri: S swell drifts SSE, persistent easterlies add lump — dawn the only window. Sat: short-period SSE swell plus small E windswells, onshore winds, morning best. — Surfline forecaster, Tue 13 Oct

wind.summary: SSW ~12 kph at 6am (cross), S/SSW ~15 kph by 9am, SE onshore from ~1pm with rain.

days.label: Today
days.note: Small, short-period NE windswell (~91 kJ, 7s) with a trace of S chop. Poor–fair everywhere, rain building. Go 6–9am on the low push before the SE onshore; a mushy groveller day.
days.surfline_text: Light to moderate S/SW winds at dawn with cleanish to bumpy conditions depending where you are - cleanest for Northern Beaches and S corners, but a lack of any real swell. It's maybe pushing waist high on the sets at the south magnets.  A bit of a pick up in short period S swell through the day and sets hitting chest high at the south magnets by the afternoon - smaller elsewhere. Winds going more onshore though for lumpy surf at all spots. Doable but unappealing. Raining as well.

days.label: Tomorrow
days.note: Strong S gusts (to ~47 kph) and a short-period S swell spike — S exposures a mess. Dee Why/Long Reef sheltered but wind-hit; Manly/Curl south corners get the size. Dawn only, low expectations.
days.surfline_text: There's going to be some strong southerly gusts out there today and decent a spike of short period S swell. South exposures will be copping the winds and swell - they'll be a well overhead to 2x OH mess so best give these a miss.  Wrap will be limited for the well sheltered Sth corners - waist high. But a bit more will get into the slightly more exposed ones, with cleanish faces and maybe chest to head surf. Might be worth trading a bit of quality for a bit more size.  Easing a bit for PM.

dee-why.window: Strong southerly gusts (30–47 kph) overnight/dawn, easing to ~25 kph by 9am but still S. Sheltered from the S spike but wrap is limited. Tide 4:31am low, 11:05am high (1.6m). Likely a bumpy, wind-hit day — dawn is the only shot.

long-reef.window: S gale and short-period S spike; limited wrap, wind-hammered. Probably skip.

curl-curl.window: Slightly more exposed corners get chest to head with cleanish faces per Surfline; strong S gusts though. South end only, dawn.

manly.window: Sth corners get chest-to-head with cleanish faces; S gusts 25–45 kph. The best bet of the four if you want size — but trading quality for size.

days.label: Weekend
days.note: Short-period SSE swell plus small E windswells, onshore winds. Waist to chest on most beaches, bigger at the Sth magnets. Morning is the best shot.
days.surfline_text: Short period SSE swell is joined by some small small easterly windswells. Sth magnets will still be picking up the most size - in the head to overhead range. Most other beaches will be waist to chest.  We're still going to be battling the onshore winds - best chance for something more appealing will be in the morning.

dee-why.window: Weekend (Sat 17 – Sun 18): SSE short-period swell plus small E windswells; E/SE onshore. Morning is the best chance.

long-reef.window: Waist to chest at best with onshore E winds; morning only.

curl-curl.window: Waist to chest; south end picks up most. Morning is the pick.

manly.window: Sth magnets/corners pick up head-high SSE per Surfline; Manly the likelier to have size. Onshore all day — dawn.
